stem: In the context of newborn screening, what are TRECs (T-cell receptor excision circles) used to measure?

options.text: The production and development of new T-cells.
The levels of maternal antibodies transferred $in$ $utero$.
The oxidative burst capacity of neonatal neutrophils.
The presence of genetic mutations in the Jack 3 receptor.

explanation: TRECs are DNA byproducts created during T-cell receptor gene rearrangement; their presence indicates functional T-cell maturation in the thymus.
rationale: These circles are excision products formed during the VDJ recombination process in the thymus.

optionExplanations.A: TRECs are DNA byproducts created during T-cell receptor gene rearrangement; their presence indicates functional T-cell maturation in the thymus.
optionExplanations.B: Newborn screening for SCID focuses on the infant's own cellular immune production, not passively acquired maternal $IgG$.
optionExplanations.C: TRECs are specific to the lymphoid lineage (T-cells) and do not provide information on myeloid cells like neutrophils.
optionExplanations.D: While Jack 3 defects cause SCID, TRECs measure the functional output of T-cell production rather than specific genetic mutations.
